## Purpose and Entry Points
This repository is a Terraform module collection for provisioning AWS IAM resources. Consumers select a focused module under `modules/` via a Terraform `source` path; there is no application runtime or central executable. Working configurations are demonstrated in `examples/*/main.tf`, while bulk/multi-instance entry points are provided by `wrappers/`.

## Terraform Composition Model
Each module follows Terraform’s input → resources/policy documents → outputs boundary:
- Inputs and provider/version contracts: `modules/iam-role/variables.tf`, `modules/iam-role/versions.tf`
- Resource and IAM-policy construction: `modules/iam-role/main.tf`
- Values exported to calling Terraform configurations: `modules/iam-role/outputs.tf`

Terraform plans and applies these configurations through the AWS provider, creating or updating AWS IAM APIs and account-scoped resources.

## Core IAM Resource Modules
Independent modules model primary AWS IAM object types:
- Account alias and password policy: `modules/iam-account/main.tf`
- Groups, memberships, managed-policy attachments, and optional self-management permissions: `modules/iam-group/main.tf`, `modules/iam-group/migrations.tf`
- Customer-managed policies from supplied JSON: `modules/iam-policy/main.tf`
- Allow-list-based read-only policies: `modules/iam-read-only-policy/main.tf`
- IAM users and optional credentials/login material: `modules/iam-user/main.tf`, `modules/iam-user/migrations.tf`

Inputs are declarative Terraform values; outputs expose created IDs, ARNs, and related attributes for composition with other AWS resources.

## Identity Federation and Trust Boundaries
Federation is separated from role assignment:
- OIDC provider registration creates the AWS trust anchor for external issuers: `modules/iam-oidc-provider/main.tf`
- General roles generate trust policies for AWS principals, services, GitHub OIDC, or SAML and attach supplied policies: `modules/iam-role/main.tf`, `modules/iam-role/variables.tf`
- The role module may also create an instance profile, bridging IAM roles to compute workloads.

OIDC provider URLs, certificate thumbprints, SAML provider ARNs, principals, subject patterns, and conditions are security-critical inputs crossing from external identity systems into AWS IAM trust policies.

## EKS Service-Account Roles
`modules/iam-role-for-service-accounts/` specializes role creation for EKS IRSA. It accepts one or more OIDC providers plus namespace/service-account subjects, constructs the resulting federated trust relationship, and conditionally assembles predefined addon permissions.
- Role and trust/resource definition: `modules/iam-role-for-service-accounts/main.tf`
- Addon policy documents and attachment logic: `modules/iam-role-for-service-accounts/policies.tf`
- Feature flags and provider/service-account mappings: `modules/iam-role-for-service-accounts/variables.tf`

This is the Kubernetes-to-AWS authorization boundary; the README recommends EKS Pod Identity as the newer alternative.

## Wrappers and Consumer Examples
Wrappers expose each module as a repeatable, map-driven aggregation layer, suitable when callers need multiple instances of the same IAM object type:
- `wrappers/iam-role/main.tf`
- `wrappers/iam-user/main.tf`
- `wrappers/iam-role-for-service-accounts/main.tf`

Examples are direct consumer configurations and practical integration entry points, including account, federation, role, and IRSA scenarios:
- `examples/iam-oidc-provider/main.tf`
- `examples/iam-role/main.tf`
- `examples/iam-role-for-service-accounts/main.tf`

## Delivery and Compatibility
The material runtime is Terraform plus the AWS provider; AWS IAM is the only operational external service. Terraform state is owned by the consumer, not this repository. Module version/provider constraints are localized per module, e.g. `modules/iam-account/versions.tf`. Migration files in group and user modules preserve Terraform state compatibility across resource-address changes. Release automation is defined in `.github/workflows/release.yml`.
